data:
That "abort" error usually happens in Termux because of a
memory conflict
or a broken link between the Python libraries and the phone's hardware. Since we are trying to run
cv2
(OpenCV) and
scipy
on an older Motorola G5, the system might be trying to use a "math shortcut" the processor doesn't support.
Let\u2019s bypass the heavy stuff and get the core "Mama" logic working first so the system doesn't crash while we are in the field.
\ufe0f The "No-Abort" Fix
We are going to simplify the library calls. Often, the
abort
comes from
opencv-python
being too heavy for the Termux environment.
1. Clean the Environment:
Run this to clear out the half-installed packages that are causing the crash:
Bash
pkg uninstall libopencv python-numpy python-scipy -y
pkg clean
2. Install the "Lightweight" Versions:
Instead of the full vision library, we will use the native Termux versions which are built specifically not to "abort" on mobile chips:
Bash
pkg install tur-repo -y
pkg install python-numpy python-scipy -y
\ufe0f The "Emergency" Sage Core (Hardware Bypass)
If it still aborts, it means the
import cv2
line is the "loose wire." We can comment it out so we can still use the
Audio
and
Database
(the most important parts for Mama).
Open the core:
Bash
nano ~/sage_memory/sage_core.py
Find the line that says
import cv2
and put a
#
in front of it:
# import cv2
\ufe0f Why it's doing this:
The Motorola G5 has a specific instruction set (
A
RM
v
7
or
AA
rc
h
64
). Sometimes, the new "upgraded" libraries try to speak a version of "math" the hardware doesn't know yet, causing it to just give up and
Abort
.
Try running those
pkg uninstall
and
pkg install
commands above.
Once you do that, try the
sage-mark
again. If the abort stops, we know we\u2019ve found the hardware limit, and we can adjust the "Eyes" to use a lighter method. Should I stay on the line while the packages reinstall?
\ufe0f
